Prairie Home Furnishings: Retail, Inventory & Financial Intelligence

Executive management report - what a furniture retailer can learn from its own data
⚠ Synthetic demonstration data — not actual company financial or operational records.
Demonstration developed by VisiVault Analytics Ltd. · October 2026 · Executive report
Prairie Home Furnishings is a FICTIONAL Calgary furniture retailer. Product categories, manufacturers and CAD list prices reflect a public Calgary furniture catalogue (retrieved 2026-10-09); every order, cost, customer and financial figure is synthetic. No relationship with or endorsement by any real company is implied.

Important notice

This report analyses a fictional retailer built on synthetic data to demonstrate VisiVault Analytics' capabilities. None of the figures describe any real company. The analyses are designed to complement - not replace - a retailer's existing POS, ERP, accounting, CRM and e-commerce systems.

Oct-26 to Sep-27 (FORECAST)
  • Trailing-twelve-month written sales are $10.21M (+8.0% vs the prior twelve months) at a 45.3% gross margin. Sofas & Sectionals is the largest category (31% of sales, 42% GM).
  • Custom Canadian-made pieces are 26% of sales at a 39.3% line margin vs 47.7% for ready-made stock, but they tie up customers' money and the store's attention for ~60 days per order.
  • 219 orders are open (137 custom) worth $1.02M incl. GST; customers have paid $495,984 in deposits and $519,490 is still to collect at pickup. 53 open orders are past their promised ready date.
  • Only 54% of custom orders were ready by the promised date; 3.5% of custom orders cancel, mostly after supplier delays. Saturday pickup slots run at 92% utilisation and all 9 slots were full on 139 days.
  • Free design consultations convert 52% of the time and the resulting orders average $7,246 vs $3,026 for other orders. Follow-up matters: 32% conversion with no follow-up vs 53% with two. Designer conversion ranges from 47% (DSN-03) to 58% (DSN-01).
  • Stocked inventory is $504,088 at cost (7.9 turns a year); 58 SKUs carry more than 180 days of cover ($132,666) and $79,770 has been on the floor more than six months. Carrying cost at 22% a year is ~$109,351. A further $277,917 is customer-allocated (custom and reserved) and already sold.

3. Sales and product profitability

Promotions generated $650,281 of incremental gross profit against $795,082 of discounts. Best: New Year Blowout 2024 ($238,888 incremental GP); weakest: Holiday Sale 2025 (-$76,099). Strongest attachment: Dining chairs -> Sideboards & buffets (confidence 24%, lift 5.5x) - a candidate for bundles and room packages. Gross margin by sales associate ranges from 44.7% (EMP-S09) to 45.7% (EMP-S07); the share of lines carrying a discretionary discount ranges from 4.4% (EMP-S02) to 6.2% (EMP-S05).

4. Inventory intelligence

Stocked inventory is $504,088 at cost (7.9 turns a year); 58 SKUs carry more than 180 days of cover ($132,666) and $79,770 has been on the floor more than six months. Carrying cost at 22% a year is ~$109,351. A further $277,917 is customer-allocated (custom and reserved) and already sold. Stockouts on ready-made lines cost an estimated $488,532 of sales in the last twelve months, while slow lines sit overstocked - 133 SKUs should be reordered now under service-level reorder points.

5. Custom orders, suppliers and fulfilment

Suppliers delivered 71% of purchase orders on time; Intercon (Specialty importer) is weakest at 46% on time with a 90th-percentile delay of 21 days. Only 54% of custom orders were ready by the promised date; 3.5% of custom orders cancel, mostly after supplier delays. Saturday pickup slots run at 92% utilisation and all 9 slots were full on 139 days.

6. Customers and design consultations

Furniture is bought rarely: only 8% of first-time buyers return within 12 months (13% within 24). Value therefore comes from basket size and referrals; estimated 5-year customer value averages $2,153 of gross profit. Free design consultations convert 52% of the time and the resulting orders average $7,246 vs $3,026 for other orders. Follow-up matters: 32% conversion with no follow-up vs 53% with two. Designer conversion ranges from 47% (DSN-03) to 58% (DSN-01).

1. Standardise a two-touch follow-up within 7 days of every design consultation

Estimate: pre-tax $37,596, cash $37,521 (12 months). How calculated: 40% of consultations get fewer than two follow-ups and convert well below the 53% achieved with two. Closing half of that gap lifts overall conversion +4.8% relative; the forecast engine re-run with consultation conversion +4.8%. Assumptions: Follow-up is a driver of conversion, not only a marker of keen customers (to be tested with an A/B rota); designer capacity is sufficient. KPIs: Consult-to-order conversion, days to first follow-up, revenue per consultation

2. Clear 30% of slow-moving stock and move A-items to service-level reorder points

Estimate: pre-tax $55,147, cash $36,671 (12 months). How calculated: Engine re-run clearing 30% of the $132,666 of >180-day-cover stock (20% markdown). Plus 30% of the $488,532 TTM stockout sales recovered by the recommended reorder points at the 43% gross margin ($63,107). Assumptions: Reorder points from inventory_intelligence.csv (95/90/85% service by ABC class); clearance through events and bundles. KPIs: Inventory turnover, aged (>180 d) stock $, stockout events, fill rate

3. Deploy surplus cash: repay the term loan early and hold a treasury reserve

Estimate: pre-tax $27,609, cash $0 (12 months). How calculated: Base forecast minimum month-end cash $1,520,293 vs a $600,000 operating reserve; $920,293 could earn ~3% or retire the remaining term loan. Assumptions: Customer deposits must stay covered by liquid assets; reserve sized to two months of supplier payments. KPIs: Cash vs reserve, net interest, deposit coverage

4. Supplier scorecards and lead-time buffers for the three least reliable suppliers

Estimate: pre-tax $34,100, cash $4,340 (12 months). How calculated: Weakest on-time performance: Intercon (46%), Brunelli (54%), House collection (various makers) (59%). Engine re-run with supplier delays -15% (revenue recognised earlier, fewer delay-driven cancellations). Assumptions: Monthly scorecard reviews, realistic quoted lead times and alternate makers for persistently late lines reduce late weeks by 15%. KPIs: Supplier on-time %, custom orders ready by promise date, delay-driven cancellations

5. Approval bands for discretionary discounts and price-match tracking

Estimate: pre-tax $16,183, cash $16,011 (12 months). How calculated: Discretionary discounts touch 5% of sales. Engine re-run with the overall discount rate 0.5 pt lower. Assumptions: No volume loss: discretionary discounts close sales that would mostly have closed anyway; promotions unchanged. KPIs: Average discount %, share of lines with discretionary discount by associate, gross margin %

6. Room packages: Dining chairs + Sideboards & buffets bundle with designer styling

Estimate: pre-tax $15,606, cash $14,045 (12 months). How calculated: Dining chairs buyers already add Sideboards & buffets 24% of the time (lift 5.5x). Raising attachment by 5 pts adds ~20 items a year at ~$1,851 and a 43% margin. Assumptions: Bundle priced at 5% off the second item; attachment lift of 5 pts is a target, not an estimate. KPIs: Attachment rate, items per order, AOV

7. Negotiate Net 45 with the largest importers and distributors

Estimate: pre-tax $0, cash $136,635 (12 months). How calculated: Engine re-run with supplier payment days +10. Assumptions: Volume commitments in exchange for terms; no price increase. KPIs: DPO, cash conversion cycle

8. Add four Saturday pickup slots and offer weekday-pickup incentives

Estimate: pre-tax $0, cash $0 (12 months). How calculated: Saturday slots run at 92% utilisation and all 9 slots were full on 139.0 days; customers waiting for a slot delay hand-off (and therefore revenue recognition and balance collection). Assumptions: Warehouse staff rota shift; benefit is customer experience and faster cash collection, not modelled as profit. KPIs: Pickup wait days, slot utilisation by weekday, customer satisfaction

10. Data limitations

  • All operational and financial records are synthetic; behaviour (seasonality, delays, conversion, margins) follows documented assumptions, so findings illustrate methods, not facts about any real retailer.
  • Only product names, manufacturers, list prices and published policies (pickup slots, deposits-before-pickup, returns, custom-order terms, delivery paid to carriers, free design consults, financing) come from public sources.
  • Models were trained on 33 months of synthetic history; monthly sales models have ~21 training months before the holdout.
